name: Cover star
what: You become a magazine cover: a giant masthead across the top, behind your head (your head covers part of it, as on a real cover), an issue line over it, cover lines beside your head and under your chin, and a barcode in the corner. Classic = a bold masthead in colour with white and yellow lines; editorial = a classic serif masthead in ink with elegant serif lines.
origin: MotionLab's own build after a design in Vibha Ramprakash's claude-video-effects (MIT), 2026-10-28
motion: classic: f0-f10 the masthead drops a quarter of its height into place (slow end) and fades in over 4 f; editorial: it settles from 105 % over 15 f (slow end) and fades in over 10 f, a thin rule draws out under it f4-f18 (S-curve); the issue line fades in f3-f11; the lower lines slide in from the left one after another (classic from f4.5, 2.4 f apart, 9 f each; editorial from f6, 3 f apart, 10.5 f each; slow end) and the side lines from their sides (classic from f9 beside the head; editorial from f13.5, lower right); classic: the barcode pops f12-f20 (slow end, small overshoot); while it holds the masthead grows 2.5 % (S-curve); the last 9 f everything fades and drifts out (accelerating)

tracks.name: masthead in
tracks.what: the masthead drops (classic) or settles (editorial) into place

tracks.name: lines in
tracks.what: the cover lines slide in one after another

min_why: the masthead and every cover line need about a second to land and a moment to be read
